content.text:
I’d prune repeated setup and validation permutations before creating the verification skill. The valuable coverage is already there: domain behavior, database transactions, CLI process behavior, and browser interactions. The larger gaps are that CI does not execute the suites and the browser tests use a fake API.

The static inventory found 179 Rust test attributes and approximately 90 frontend test cases. Those counts do not establish runtime cost; no tests were run for this review.

| Action | Recommendation | Tradeoff |
|---|---|---|
| Delete four low-value tests | Remove the two `SearchSimilarity` ordering tests and the standalone migration/fixture smoke tests. Repository tests already load those migrations and fixtures while asserting behavior. | Removes wrapper and scaffolding checks; confirm the database smoke tests were not intended to establish a search-path contract. |
| Consolidate CLI coverage | Move configuration permutations into in-process tests and retain representative subprocess cases. Reuse schema output within each test. | Fewer process launches while preserving checks that depend on launching the executable. |
| Move malformed-response matrices lower | Exercise public frontend loaders with injected fetch responses. Keep representative browser failure and retry cases. | Retains rejection coverage; browser coverage concentrates on user-visible behavior. |
| Separate live tests | Make Parliament API checks explicitly opt-in. Preserve historical database regressions in a separate opt-in tier. | Default tests become independent of external availability; live compatibility needs an explicit run. |

The direct deletion candidates are in [search_similarity.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/search_similarity.rs:25) and [postgres.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/postgres.rs:50). The similarity tests mostly restate primitive ordering, and the test named `does_not_round` does not exercise rounding.

The largest consolidation opportunity is [cli_config.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/cli_config.rs:34): configuration and help matrices repeatedly launch the executable. Keep process tests for boot, environment handling, output streams, exit status, and commands that must avoid database side effects. Consolidate configuration parsing separately. [cli_response_help.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/cli_response_help.rs:10) also repeatedly requests the same response schema.

For the frontend, move the malformed `match_source` and alias matrices in [search.spec.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/tests/search.spec.ts:331), and malformed detail payload matrices in [entity-details.spec.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/tests/entity-details.spec.ts:545), into tests of the public `searchEntities` and `loadDetails` boundaries. Do not export private parsers solely for testing. Remove one redundant Windows/Linux keyboard case because both exercise the same Ctrl branch; retain Mac and one Ctrl case. Merge the overlapping empty-member scenarios while preserving distinctions between zero, unknown, and failure.

Keep the resolution graph cases, scoring goldens, artifact round trips, transaction rollback/retry checks, and source portability tests. Likewise, preserve browser races, SSR, navigation, escaping, geometry, and pointer/touch cases: similar-looking tests cover different failure paths.

Two tests need correction before their coverage can be trusted. The numeric-money fixture in [entity-details.spec.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/tests/entity-details.spec.ts:704) omits the currency-group `amount`, so rejection happens before the numeric party amount is inspected. The environment test in [integration.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/integration.rs:218) omits the now-required ingestion key, so argument parsing prevents it from reaching the intended environment failure.

CI is a separate priority: [rust.yml](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/.github/workflows/rust.yml:41) runs Clippy for libraries and binaries, but executes no tests. No workflow runs frontend tests or Svelte checks. The README’s `make frontend-check` command also has no target; `make -n frontend-check` confirmed that mismatch.

After pruning, extend the existing [verification skill](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/.agents/skills/verify/SKILL.md) instead of adding a competing driver. It currently describes API snapshots and stale startup assumptions. The useful addition is a proven browser → SvelteKit → Rust → isolated database path, plus CLI workflows and teardown evidence. Today’s frontend tests run real SvelteKit against a fake HTTP API, so they cannot establish that integration.

This follows the two relevant principles: test distinct behavior at the appropriate boundary, and subtract duplication before adding another verification layer. No files were changed.
